title: Hue/Saturation: unavailable on hidden layers, a layer mask, Grayscale and Multichannel; empty-layer alert (#14749)
body:
Fixes #14749
Part of #14739

## What was wrong (main 3bc25b0ca, checked with an engine test, Hue/Saturation with saturation −50)
| Case | Reference | Before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Hidden pixel layer | greyed, "not currently available" | enabled, ran, +1 history state |
| Targeted layer mask | greyed | enabled, edited the mask, +1 state |
| Grayscale 8 / 16 bit | greyed | enabled, ran, +1 state |
| Multichannel | greyed | disabled, but only because the converted document has no active layer |
| Empty layer | "Could not complete the Hue/Saturation command because the active layer is empty.", nothing changes | ran with no error, +1 state |

Cause:
- `has_adjustable` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/adjust_cmds.rs`), shared by every adjustment, accepts any pixel layer or rendered smart object.
- `mask_target_enabled` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/channel_cmds/targeting.rs`) enables every adjustment when a layer's mask is the target.

## The fix
Same shape as Channel Mixer's refusals (#15618), limited to Hue/Saturation:
- `adjust_cmds.rs`:
  - `HUE_SATURATION_ID` and the two alert texts.
  - `hue_saturation_enabled_with(s, p)`: by the Channels panel's target. A layer mask is refused. A filter mask keeps its own check. Alpha channel and Quick Mask keep `has_adjustable`. On pixels, 8- and 16-bit Grayscale documents, Multichannel documents and a hidden pixel layer are refused, and everything else is `has_adjustable`.
  - `hue_saturation_target_enabled(s)`: the menu's enabled check.
  - `hue_saturation_refusal(s, p)`: the run-time refusal, which adds the empty-layer alert.
- `cmd.rs`:
  - The adjustments table's `enabled:` becomes `match kind { "hueSaturation" => hue_saturation_target_enabled, _ => has_adjustable }`.
  - `run` calls `hue_saturation_refusal` first for `hueSaturation`.
  - The new test module is declared.
- `targeting.rs`: `mask_target_enabled` returns Hue/Saturation's own check for that command, so a targeted mask no longer enables it.

Kept as before:
- Lock transparent pixels, CMYK, Lab, Indexed, 16- and 32-bit RGB and smart objects (as a smart filter) keep working. So does 32-bit Grayscale: #14749 measured Grayscale at 8 and 16 bit only.
- Lock image pixels and Lock all stay refused when the adjustment runs, as before.
- Alpha-channel and Quick Mask targets, a layer inside a hidden group and a hidden smart object (not measured) keep today's checks.
- The other Image › Adjustments commands are unchanged.

## Tests (Windows 11, local, engine crate)
New file `crates/engine/src/cmd/hue_saturation_enabled_tests.rs`, checked against the issue's "Done when" list. "Without the fix" means `cmd.rs` and `targeting.rs` as on main, with the new functions left in place so the tests compile:

| Test | Without the fix | With the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `a_hidden_pixel_layer_refuses_hue_saturation` | fails: "Hue/Saturation is greyed" | passes |
| `a_targeted_layer_mask_refuses_hue_saturation` (Channels-panel target and an explicit `"target":"mask"`) | fails | passes |
| `grayscale_and_multichannel_documents_refuse_hue_saturation` (8 and 16 bit, also with Colorize; Multichannel) | fails at Grayscale 8 bit | passes |
| `an_empty_layer_stops_with_the_empty_layer_alert` (exact text, no history state) | fails: the command ran | passes |
| `hue_saturation_keeps_working_where_it_worked` (visible layer, Lock transparent pixels, RGB 16/32, CMYK, Lab, Indexed, smart object) | passes (guard) | passes |
| `a_32_bit_grayscale_document_keeps_hue_saturation` (also with Colorize; added in 2639c8da1) | fails if 32-bit Grayscale is refused too: "Grayscale 32 bit: Hue/Saturation is available" | passes |
| `locked_pixels_stay_refused` (Lock image pixels, Lock all) | passes (guard) | passes |
| `the_other_adjustments_keep_todays_behaviour` (Brightness/Contrast on a hidden layer and in Grayscale) | passes (guard) | passes |

Also ran, with the fix:
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib adjust`: 105 passed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib channel_cmds`: 66 passed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib hue`: 13 passed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: passed.
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Cargo's only warnings are the existing unused workspace dependencies, which have nothing to do with this change.

At 2639c8da1 (32-bit Grayscale kept), on Linux (ljkx/ci-runner):
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine-core -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p photocraft-engine-core -E 'test(hue_saturation) | test(adjust)'`: 136 passed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --features egui/serde,egui/persistence,toml/display --lib -- adjust_preview`: 17 passed. The two preview parity tests skip Hue/Saturation only in 8- and 16-bit Grayscale. If 32-bit Grayscale is refused too, both fail: "hueSaturation Grayscale F32 …: command and preview disagree on validity".

Not run: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 target here; nothing platform-specific changed), and the app's menu (it reads the same `enabled` check).

## Merging with the other refusal PRs
Trial merges of this branch with each PR head. The conflicts are all "keep both": each PR adds its own arm or block at the same spot.
- **#15618 (Channel Mixer):**
  - `cmd.rs`: one `match kind` with both arms (`"channelMixer"`, `"hueSaturation"`, `_ => has_adjustable`), and both `if kind == …` refusal calls in `run`.
  - `adjust_cmds.rs`: keep both blocks of constants and functions after `has_adjustable`.
  - `targeting.rs`: keep both early returns in `mask_target_enabled`.
- **#15019 (Gradient Map):**
  - `cmd.rs`: its `if kind == "gradientMap" { … } else { … }` becomes a third arm of the same `match`.
  - `adjust_cmds.rs`: keep both blocks after `has_adjustable`.
- **#14790** (Hue/Saturation parameter ranges, `adjust_params.rs`): merges cleanly.
- The test module is declared after the `history_*` modules, away from where #15618 and #15019 declare theirs.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Hue/Saturation is unavailable for hidden pixel layers, layer masks, targeted masks, and pixel targets in 8- or 16-bit Grayscale and Multichannel documents. Supported 32-bit Grayscale targets remain available.
  * The adjustment reports an error for raster layers with no visible content, including fully erased layers, and refuses unsupported locked targets.
  * Other adjustments retain their existing availability on hidden layers and in Grayscale.
  * Refused adjustments do not add history or produce a preview in the affected cases.
